question: In acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis (APSGN), serum C3 is characteristically low while C4 remains normal, and haematuria typically appears 1–3 weeks after a pharyngeal infection.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. APSGN is characterised by low C3 with normal C4 (alternative pathway activation), and a latent period of 1–3 weeks after pharyngitis — a key distinguishing feature from synpharyngitic haematuria seen in IgA nephropathy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. APSGN activates the alternative complement pathway, selectively depressing C3 (not C4). The latent period of 1–3 weeks (pharyngitis) or 3–6 weeks (skin infection) distinguishes it from IgA nephropathy where haematuria is concurrent with infection.
